description.from:
Requested by Ryan (2026-10-31): put Papyrus on Amazon Alexa, built the way a real, published, certified skill has to be built, so it works on our two Echo Shows and on anyone else's.

Goal: a person says "Alexa, open <publication>" and hears and sees the latest stories. Echo Show devices show them on screen. A person who links their account gets the signed-in experience: their own reference feed, and Accept/Reject votes that train the site's Cyclotron.

Decisions in this plan (change them here if Ryan disagrees):
- One skill per Papyrus site, generated from site config, with the publication as the invocation name. This follows the config-only-per-site rule and each site's own Cognito pool. Pilot site: Pilobolus (pre-production). Anth.us goes last.
- The skill is a Papyrus plugin (amplify/plugins/alexa), like newsletter and reader-steering: a Lambda endpoint in the site backend, off unless the site turns it on.
- Sign-in uses Alexa's standard OAuth account linking (authorization code grant + PKCE) against a new Alexa app client on the site's Cognito pool. The Google provider is the only one. When a request needs a linked account, an Echo Show shows Amazon's own QR code, so the "scan to sign in" experience needs no custom flow. The CLI remote-login broker is not reused: certification expects standard account linking.
- Readers can use the public parts without linking. Account linking is optional, not mandatory.
- The skill package (manifest, interaction model, APL documents) lives in Git and ships through the pipeline. Nobody edits it by hand in the developer console.

Milestones (one epic each, in order):
1. Skill foundation: voice-only public stories, in development stage on our own Echos.
2. Echo Show screens: APL feed and story views.
3. Account linking: Cognito Alexa client, Google sign-in, QR linking on the Show.
4. Signed-in newsroom: personal reference feed and voice Accept/Reject votes.
5. Certification and publishing: pass Amazon review and go live for the pilot site.
6. Rollout to every site: config-only, Anth.us last.
7. Listen to full stories: long-form audio playback (follow-up after the first publication).

Ryan's own steps (I can't do these): own the Amazon Developer account and authorise the ASK CLI once for CI; approve the Cognito and backend deploys; create a dedicated Google test account for Amazon's certification testers (never a Cognito password user); submit for certification if the console requires the account owner.

Sources: developer.amazon.com account-linking requirements (updated 2026-02-04) and "How users experience account linking" (QR code on screen devices).

Every behaviour change ships with Gherkin specs. The last task is a p.apyr.us docs page.

Every behaviour change ships with Gherkin specs. The last task is a p.apyr.us docs page.

## Confirmed by Ryan (2026-10-31)
- One skill per site: confirmed.
- Rollout order: Pilobolus (pilot), then Shipped, then Distinctive Mark, then the rest. Anth.us last.
- Signing in is optional: confirmed.
- Built as a Papyrus plugin (`plugins: ["alexa"]` in a site's papyrus.config.ts): confirmed.
- Implementation decision: the skill's Lambda is TypeScript, bundled by Amplify `defineFunction` (ask-sdk-core, aws-jwt-verify, and the Markus TS parser for SSML/APL text). The Python plugin functions are bundled with no dependencies, and Cognito JWT verification needs a crypto library.

## Execution plan (waves)

Wave 0, contracts (one PR, sequential): PPY-dc7748 "Alexa contracts". It sets up the plugin skeleton, the config schema, the handler module layout with typed seams (content source, auth, APL, SSML, intents registry), the skill-package generator skeleton, the feature-file skeletons and the npm script hooks. After it merges, every later task only ADDS files in its own folder. Shared files (registry.ts, package.json, tests.yml, the intents index) are touched in wave 0 only.

Wave 1, in parallel (one worktree and one PR each, separate folders):
- A. Intents + SSML + public content source (PPY-55bf5b)
- B. Skill-package generator + ASK CLI deploy step, inert until the LWA secret exists (PPY-c82bd1)
- C. APL feed, story and viewport profiles (PPY-fec649, PPY-d27478, PPY-33162d)
- D. Token validation + LinkAccount cards (PPY-39ed30)
- E. Alexa Cognito app client CDK, gated by the plugin (PPY-2a34d4). Critical path for the spike.
- F. Privacy and terms pages for the listing (PPY-7ddf37)

Wave 2, after wave 1 and Ryan's steps:
- Pilobolus in development stage (PPY-6a1047). Evidence from `ask smapi simulate-skill` plus Ryan on the Echo Shows.
- Linking spike on the real device (PPY-ce567f), then the account-linking manifest (PPY-81e6f9).
- In parallel: personal feed (PPY-d1ca49), Accept/Reject (PPY-46a89a), docs page (PPY-8f3d31).

Wave 3: certification for Pilobolus (PPY-39a24e, PPY-11a4d3). Then M6 site by site: Shipped, Distinctive Mark, the others, Anth.us last. Certification submissions for different sites can overlap. M7 audio (two tasks in parallel) after the first publication.

## Worktree and disk rules for every implementing agent
- Disk had 25 GB free on 2026-10-31. At most 6 Alexa worktrees at once, under ~/Projects/Papyrus-worktrees/alexa-<slug>, branched from origin/develop. Remove each one as soon as its PR merges.
- Never `npm install`/`npm ci` in a worktree: `ln -s ~/Projects/Papyrus/node_modules node_modules`. Only the wave 0 PR adds npm dependencies, and the main checkout is then updated once.
- Never `poetry install` or `poetry run` in a worktree (that makes a new venv per worktree). Use the main checkout's venv interpreter directly when Python is needed.
- Local checks are targeted only: typecheck, lint on touched files, and the agent's own feature files and test scripts. No `npm run build`, no full BDD suites and no Amplify sandbox locally. GitHub Actions CI is the full gate, and it runs remotely at no disk cost.
- Board-only changes go straight to develop. Code goes through PR, green CI, then a merge commit.
